new_statements.relation_note: The catalog holds Yil with an empty rule (qs-tier-2026-09-12) and no existing statements. This source supplies the placement (initial by default), the schwa-avoidance condition and the minimal pair; it neither agrees nor contradicts because the catalog recorded no placement. Note: extracted text drops the /ə/ and /ɨ/ glyphs (they come out as '…' or '//'); the quote was read from the page render, where the prose has /ə/ and the pair is written with barred i (ɨ).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default stress on the first syllable of the word. When the first syllable contains the reduced vowel /ə/ (written <ɨ> in the orthography, as the example pair and the transcribed passage on p. 3 show), stress normally moves off it, since /ə/ tends to be unstressed; but the pair ɨ'ngati 'I bury a man' vs 'ɨngati 'I hurry' shows that a first-syllable /ə/ can carry stress in some words, which is why the author calls stress 'probably phonemic'. So: initial by default, schwa-avoiding, with a residue of lexical contrast confined to schwa-initial words.
new_statements.exceptions: Words whose first syllable has /ə/: stress usually not initial there; one contrastive pair (ɨ'ngati vs 'ɨngati) shows stress on /ə/ is possible, so the author hedges 'probably phonemic'. No tone and no length statement despite the section title.
new_statements.identity_note: The OPD is headed 'Yil Language [YLL], Lumi – Sandaun Province; Torricelli Phylum; Wapei-Palei Stock; Wapei Family; population 3280 (1979); major villages Wublagil, Sikel, Eikil, Laingim, Pimon'. No dialect is specified; the data are credited to Martens & Tuominen 1977. It also notes that in Au (same family) the fricative /ɣ/ is written <h>, but says nothing about Au stress.

The SIL Yil OPD held by the project (n.d., printed 2004, not a listed work here) restates the same: 'Stress is probably phonemic. Usually it falls on the first syllable, except when /ə/ occurs in the first syllable' and cites the same 'I bury a man'/'I hurry' pair.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress (with tone and length) is stated to be non-phonemic; word stress normally falls on the first syllable. Full vowels carry more intensity than /ə/; when the first syllable has /ə/ and the next syllable a full vowel, stress (and length) may shift to the second syllable or the two syllables may be equally stressed. In the Residue the authors flag one apparent stress minimal pair in verbs ([ə'ŋati] 'I bury a man' vs ['əŋati] 'I hurry') and leave open whether this is sentence stress, incipient phonemic stress/length, or syllabic consonants.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing on secondary stress; only the remark that a schwa first syllable and a following full-vowel syllable 'may have equal stress'.
new_statements.exceptions: Schwa-initial words: stress can move to the second syllable (or level stress) when syllable 1 has /ə/ and syllable 2 a full vowel. Residue 6.1: possible contrastive stress in certain verbs (one pair given), status undetermined.
new_statements.identity_note: Tuominen & Martens 1977 is based on c. 900 words collected in Mampel village (Lumi sub-province, West Sepik), Aug-Oct 1974; Yil is said to be spoken by c. 2100 people in twelve villages. No dialect differentiation is discussed.
